source_note: Checked against the full texts read in my blind round (Kendler: PMC3556483 page text including Tables 1-6 and the MathJax chi-square values; Pennington: saved publisher HTML text plus the vignette and Table 1 read from screenshots). No browser tab was needed.

results.note: All figures match (78,079 = 27,241 + 7,301 + 43,537; 51,208 = 36,230 + 14,978). 'By age 10/5' and 'mean 4.4 years' rest on a census-based upper-bound estimate of age at first cohabitation (Methods › Sample).

results.corrected_extracted: A register record of drug problems (the study's 'drug abuse': drug use disorder or drug psychosis diagnoses, convictions under Crime Register codes 5011 and 5012 for crimes related to drug abuse (crimes related only to alcohol, or only to trafficking in or possession of drugs, excluded) or long-term high-volume collection of prescribed sedatives, hypnotics or opioids; alcohol and tobacco excluded) in 4.5% (95% CI 4.2–4.8) of adoptees (820 people) against 2.9% in all of Sweden for the same birth years; cases came from hospital discharge (527), crime (313), outpatient (264), prescribed drug (118) and primary care (8) registers, with overlap.
results.corrected_locator: Results › General description, 1st paragraph; Methods › Outcome variable, 1st–4th paragraphs
results.note: Numbers confirmed (820/18,115 = 4.5%; register counts sum to 1,230, hence overlap). The definition sits in Outcome variable paragraphs 1–3, and 'drug-related convictions' was broader than the paper's: codes 5011/5012, crimes only about alcohol, trafficking or possession excluded.

Matches Methodological limitations 3rd–4th paragraphs and Table 5 (0.96, 0.93–0.98, P<.01; adjusted 1.00, 0.96–1.02; interaction P=.88). The univariate association was significantly negative, not merely non-positive; AFCAP is a census-based upper-bound estimate.

RQ2 paragraph: reward d .15 (−.02 to .31) inconclusive, punishment .007 (−.16 to .17) equivalent. Table 1: brain-disease readers gave slightly more reward (253.39 vs 244.20 pence; p = .03, above the study's α of .01).

1,578 (789 per factor level) for ±0.20; ±0.28 (n = 392) and ±0.30 (n = 362) come from the smallest cells. The drug-use-arm restriction is stated in Results (Research Questions 2–3); cells also reflect manipulation-check exclusions.

Matches Discussion paragraphs 2 and 6 and Conclusions. 'In agreement with two earlier studies' is the authors' reading: Kelly et al. (2021) had no comparison health condition (Introduction, 6th paragraph). The functional-attribution idea is offered, not tested.
